newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs to drift off, target 135.80 support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs to drift off, target 135.80 support.

text.p: September BTPs will drift lower in the near term towards support at 135.80, but the longer term bull trend remains intact, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
They added the market would struggle to move up independently of Bunds, with the 10-year spread near record lows under 100 basis points.
"We're waiting for Bunds," said one trader at an Italian bank in London. "But the one week objective is still 136.70."
The trader put good support at 136.00, then 135.80. Charts show the market hit a daily high of 135.84 last Friday.
"But every support is a buying opportunity," he said.
Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking, said if BTPs did see a correction, it would be fairly major.
"The market's still overbought, but it has been for ages. Having rallied eight points without a correction, you have to ask when you're going to get one," he said.
Ostwald put support at 135.84, the high from last Friday, followed by a prop at 135.33/35. The market hit a low of 135.33 on Monday and 135.35 last Friday.
"But a major setback would see the market trading down to congestion at 134.70,74," he said.
"If we don't push up much further on Bunds, this market has to come back because I don't see many people buying the spread at 100 basis points," Ostwald added.
By 0826 GMT, September BTPs were down 11 basis points at 136.13. The 10-year BTP/Bund spread was at 99 basis points.
Ostwald put initial resistance at Monday's high of 136.40, followed by 136.60, the first resistance on pivot point analysis, then 137.00.
"For the moment the momentum is with it. The trend's your friend," he said.
September Eurolira was down two basis points at 93.46.
